title: The declared SHAPE of one bounded position artifact -- what each section holds, where it comes from, where it cools to, and who it is for (ADR-020 decision 3)
description: A bounded artifact that carries POSITION is under a ceiling, and everything under a ceiling eventually competes for it. The sections of such an artifact are therefore not knowledge of a writer: they are ROWS of this declaration, and each row states four things about one section -- the truth that lives there (`holds`), whether it is authored or projected (`source`), the record KIND a cold span of it belongs to (`cools_to`), and who it is written for (`audience`). Nothing here executes: there is no branch, no path to a destination, no order of operations and no behaviour of any kind, so this document can be stored, diffed, versioned and generated by a machine that will never run it (Cardinal IV). The passage that carries a span out of a section reads `cools_to` and knows no section name, which is what makes a new section a ROW rather than an edit to a writer, and a new destination a ROW rather than a branch. A section that declares NO `cools_to` is legal and is a statement, not an omission: it says that nothing in this section cools -- a span cut from it stays in the journal, is counted as unlanded, and the passage refuses to guess a home for it, because a destination guessed under pressure is exactly the improvisation this mechanism replaces. The kit ships this grammar and no rows: which sections a host's position artifact has is the host's declaration, and a framework that shipped a section set would have decided the shape of somebody else's steering surface before meeting it.

id.description: What this shape is called. One shape per bounded artifact, identified so that two declarations of one artifact are refused as two homes for one truth rather than merged.

artifact.description: The bounded artifact this is the shape OF, as a host-relative path -- the same path the eviction record carries, so an event and the shape that governed it can be read together. Declared HERE and asked of no caller: a passage told both the shape and the artifact separately could be handed a pair that do not belong to each other, and would then journal a landing under the wrong surface's name.

summary.description: What this artifact is for, in the host's own words. Prose for a reader; nothing resolves it.

sections.description: The sections of the artifact, in the order the host declares them. An EMPTY list is legal and is the honest state of an artifact whose shape has not been declared yet: nothing is wrong with such an artifact, no gate fires on it, and the one consequence is that no span of it can cool until a row says where to.

id.description: The section, as the writer addresses it -- the same word an eviction event carries in its `section` field. A row nobody can match to a section governs nothing.

holds.description: The one truth that lives in this section. A section that holds two truths is two sections wearing one heading, and it is the state in which a ceiling begins to trade one of them for the other.

source.description: Where this section's content COMES FROM -- a row of the record-keeping vocabulary's `section_sources`, never an enum spelled here. It is the statement that decides whether a hand may write here at all, and it is declared before anything is projected, so the day a section becomes a projection is a change to this row and not to a writer.

cools_to.description: The record KIND a cold span of this section belongs to -- a row of the record-keeping vocabulary's `kinds`, which is a WORD and never a path: where records of that kind live is the corpus map's answer, and a destination spelled as a path here would be a second home for it. OPTIONAL, and its absence is a declaration: this section has no cold form, so a span cut from it is preserved in the journal, counted as unlanded, and never carried anywhere by guess.

audience.description: Who this section is written FOR -- a row of the record-keeping vocabulary's `audiences`. A section whose reader is unstated is written for whoever happens to open the artifact, and under a ceiling that reader is the one who decides what to cut.
